content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Domum Dei decet sanctitúdo: * Sponsum eius Christum adorémus in ea.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Sponsum eius Christum adorémus in ea.
content.english: Ant. In her let us worship her Bridegroom, even Christ.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Domum Dei decet sanctitúdo: * Sponsum eius Christum adorémus in ea.
content.english: Ant. Holiness becometh the house of God. * In her let us worship her Bridegroom, even Christ.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Sponsum eius Christum adorémus in ea.
content.english: Ant. In her let us worship her Bridegroom, even Christ.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
content.english: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

content.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
content.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

content.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?
content.english: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

content.latin: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.
content.english: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

content.latin: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
content.english: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

content.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
content.english: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

content.latin: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

content.latin: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
content.english: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

content.latin: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

content.latin: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

content.english: Psalm 45 [2]

content.latin: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adiútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
content.english: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

content.latin: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
content.english: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

content.latin: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine eius.
content.english: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

content.latin: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
content.english: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

content.latin: 45:6 Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur: * adiuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
content.english: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

content.latin: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
content.english: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

content.latin: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.
content.english: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

content.latin: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
content.english: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

content.latin: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
content.english: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

content.latin: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
content.english: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

content.latin: 45:12 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.
content.english: 45:12 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

content.latin: Psalmus 47 [3]
content.english: Psalm 47 [3]

content.latin: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto eius.
content.english: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised * in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

content.latin: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
content.english: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

content.latin: 47:4 Deus in dómibus eius cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
content.english: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

content.latin: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
content.english: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

content.latin: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
content.english: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

content.latin: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
content.english: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

content.latin: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
content.english: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

content.latin: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
content.english: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

content.latin: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * iustítia plena est déxtera tua.
content.english: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

content.latin: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Iudæ: * propter iudícia tua, Dómine.
content.english: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

content.latin: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus eius.
content.english: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

content.latin: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte eius: * et distribúite domos eius, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
content.english: 47:14 Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.

content.latin: 47:15 Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
content.english: 47:15 For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.

content.english: ℣. Holiness becometh thine house, O Lord.

content.latin: ℟. In longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: ℟. For ever.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De libro secundo Paralipómenon
content.english: Lesson from the book of Paralipomenon

content.latin: 1 Cum complésset Sálomon fundens preces, ignis descéndit de cælo et devorávit holocáusta et víctimas: et maiéstas Dómini implévit domum.
content.english: 1 And when Solomon had made an end of his prayer, fire came down from heaven, and consumed the holocausts and the victims: and the majesty of the Lord filled the house.

content.latin: 2 Nec póterant sacerdótes íngredi templum Dómini, eo quod implésset maiéstas Dómini, templum Dómini.
content.english: 2 Neither could the priests enter into the temple of the Lord, because the majesty of the Lord had filled the temple of the Lord.

content.latin: 3 Sed et omnes fílii Israël vidébant descendéntem ignem, et glóriam Dómini super domum: et corruéntes proni in terram super paviméntum stratum lápide, adoravérunt et laudavérunt Dóminum: Quóniam bonus, quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 3 Moreover all the children of Israel saw the fire coming down, and the glory of the Lord upon the house: and falling down with their faces to the ground, upon the stone pavement, they adored and praised the Lord: because he is good, because his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 4 Rex autem et omnis pópulus immolábant víctimas coram Dómino.
content.english: 4 And the king and all the people sacrificed victims before the Lord.

content.latin: 5 Mactávit ígitur rex Sálomon hóstias, boum vigínti duo míllia, aríetum centum vigínti míllia: et dedicávit domum Dei rex et univérsus pópulus.
content.english: 5 And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand oxen, and one hundred and twenty thousand rams: and the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. In dedicatióne templi decantábat pópulus laudem:
content.english: ℟. When the Temple was dedicated the people sang praise;

content.latin: * Et in ore eórum dulcis resonábat sonus.
content.english: * And sweet in their mouths was the sound.

content.latin: ℣. Fundáta est domus Dómini supra vérticem móntium, et vénient ad eam omnes gentes.
content.english: ℣. The Lord's house is established in the top of the mountains; and all nations shall flow unto it.

content.latin: ℟. Et in ore eórum dulcis resonábat sonus.
content.english: ℟. And sweet in their mouths was the sound.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 6 Sacerdótes autem stabant in offíciis suis, et Levítæ in organis cárminum Dómini, quæ fecit David rex ad laudándum Dóminum: Quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius; hymnos David canéntes per manus suas: porro sacerdótes canébant tubis ante eos, cunctúsque Israël stabat.
content.english: 6 And the priests stood in their offices: and the Levites with the instruments of music of the Lord, which king David made to praise the Lord: because his mercy endureth for ever, singing the hymns of David by their ministry: and the priests sounded with trumpets before them, and all Israel stood.

content.latin: 7 Sanctificávit quoque Sálomon médium átrii ante templum Dómini: obtúlerat enim ibi holocáusta, et ádipes pacificórum: quia altáre ǽneum, quod fécerat, non póterat sustinére holocáusta et sacrifícia et ádipes.
content.english: 7 Solomon also sanctified the middle of the court before the temple of the Lord: for he offered there the holocausts, and the fat of the peace offerings: because the brazen altar, which he had made, could not hold the holocausts and the sacrifices and the fat:

content.latin: 8 Fecit ergo Sálomon solemnitátem in témpore illo septem diébus, et omnis Israël cum eo, ecclésia magna valde ab intróitu Emath usque ad Torréntem Ægýpti.
content.english: 8 And Solomon kept the solemnity at that time seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great congregation, from the entrance of Emath to the torrent of Egypt.

content.latin: 9 Fecítque die octávo colléctam, eo quod dedicásset altáre septem diébus, et solemnitátem celebrásset diébus septem.
content.english: 9 And he made on the eighth day a solemn assembly, because he had kept the dedication of the altar seven days, and had celebrated the solemnity seven days.

content.latin: * Et vénient ad eam omnes gentes, et dicent: Glória tibi, Dómine.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: 11 Complevítque Sálomon domum Dómini, et domum regis, et ómnia quæ disposúerat in corde suo, ut fáceret in domo Dómini et in domo sua, et prosperátus est.
content.english: 11 And Solomon finished the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all that he had designed in his heart to do, in the house of the Lord, and in his own house, and he prospered.

content.latin: 12 Appáruit autem ei Dóminus nocte, et ait: Audívi oratiónem tuam, et elégi locum istum mihi in domum sacrifícii.
content.english: 12 And the Lord appeared to him by night, and said: I have heard thy prayer, and I have chosen this place to myself for a house of sacrifice.

content.latin: 13 Si cláusero cælum, et plúvia non flúxerit, et mandávero et præcépero locústæ, ut dévoret terram, et mísero pestiléntiam in pópulum meum:
content.english: 13 If I shut up heaven, and there fall no rain, or if I give orders, and command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people:

content.latin: 14 Convérsus autem pópulus meus, super quos invocátum est nomen meum, deprecátus me fúerit, et exquisíerit fáciem meam, et égerit pœniténtiam a viis suis pessimis: et ego exáudiam de cælo, et propítius ero peccátis eórum, et sanábo terram eórum.
content.english: 14 And my people, upon whom my name is called, being converted, shall make supplication to me, and seek out my face, and do penance for their most wicked ways: then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sins and will heal their land.

content.latin: 15 Oculi quoque mei erunt apérti, et aures meæ eréctæ ad oratiónem eius qui in loco isto oráverit.
content.english: 15 My eyes also shall be open, and my ears attentive to the prayer of him that shall pray in this place.

content.latin: 16 Elégi enim et sanctificávi locum istum, ut sit nomen meum ibi in sempitérnum, et permáneant óculi mei et cor meum ibi cunctis diébus.
content.english: 16 For I have chosen, and have sanctified this place, that my name may be there for ever, and my eyes and my heart may remain there perpetually.

content.latin: 83:2 Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.
content.english: 83:2 How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! * my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord.

content.english: 83:4 Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, * my king and my God.

content.english: 83:5 Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: * they shall praise thee for ever and ever.

content.latin: 83:11 Quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis, * super míllia.

content.latin: 83:11 Elégi abiéctus esse in domo Dei mei: * magis quam habitáre in tabernáculis peccatórum.
content.english: 83:11 I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God, * rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.

content.latin: 83:12 Quia misericórdiam, et veritátem díligit Deus: * grátiam et glóriam dabit Dóminus.
content.english: 83:12 For God loveth mercy and truth: * the Lord will give grace and glory.

content.english: 83:13 He will not deprive of good things them that walk in innocence: * O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.

content.latin: 87:2 Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: * in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.

content.latin: 87:3 Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:
content.english: 87:3 Let my prayer come in before thee: * incline thy ear to my petition.

content.english: 87:4 For my soul is filled with evils: * and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.

content.latin: 87:5 Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adiutório, inter mórtuos liber.
content.english: 87:5 I am counted among them that go down to the pit: * I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.

content.english: 87:6 Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: * and they are cast off from thy hand.

content.english: 87:8 Thy wrath is strong over me: * and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.

content.english: 87:9 Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: * they have set me an abomination to themselves.

content.english: 87:9 I was delivered up, and came not forth: * my eyes languished through poverty.

content.latin: 87:11 Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
content.english: 87:11 Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? * or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?

content.latin: 87:12 Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
content.english: 87:12 Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: * and thy truth in destruction?

content.latin: 87:13 Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et iustítia tua in terra obliviónis?
content.english: 87:13 Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; * and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?

content.latin: 87:14 Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.

content.latin: 87:15 Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?
content.english: 87:15 Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: * why turnest thou away thy face from me?

content.latin: 87:18 Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.

content.latin: 87:19 Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.

content.latin: Sermo 252 de Tempore
content.english: 252nd for the Season.

content.latin: Quotiescúmque, fratres caríssimi, altáris vel templi festivitátem cólimus, si fidéliter ac diligénter atténdimus et sancte ac iuste vívimus, quidquid in templis manufáctis ágitur, totum in nobis spiritáli ædificatióne complétur. Non enim mentítus est ille qui dixit: Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos; et íterum: Nescitis quia córpora vestra templum sunt Spíritus Sancti, qui in vobis est? Et ideo, fratres caríssimi, quia, nullis præcedéntibus méritis, per grátiam Dei merúimus fíeri templum Dei, quantum possumus cum ipsíus adiutório labóremus, ne Dóminus noster in templo suo, hoc est, in nobis ipsis, invéniat quod óculos suæ maiestátis offéndat.
content.english: Dearly beloved brethren, as often as we keep the Dedication-Feast of some Altar or Church, if we think faithfully and carefully, and live holily and righteously, that which is done in temples made with hands, is done in our soul by a spiritual building. He at the Dedication of the Temple. lied not who said: The temple of God is holy; which temple ye are i Cor. iii. 17, and again: Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost, Which is in you, vi. 19. And therefore, dearly beloved brethren, since by the grace of God, without any foregoing deserts of our own, we have been made meet to become the Temple of God, let us work as hard as we can, with His help, that our Lord may not find in His Temple, that is, in us, anything to offend the eyes of His Majesty.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Orántibus in loco isto,
content.english: ℟. If they pray toward this place,

content.latin: * Dimítte peccáta pópuli tui, Deus, et osténde eis viam bonam per quam ámbulent, et da glóriam in loco isto.
content.english: * Forgive the sin of thy people, O God, and teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and manifest forth thy glory in this place.

content.latin: ℣. Qui regis Israël inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Ioseph, qui sedes super Chérubim.
content.english: ℣. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock, thou that sittest upon the cherubim.

content.latin: ℟. Dimítte peccáta pópuli tui, Deus, et osténde eis viam bonam per quam ámbulent, et da glóriam in loco isto.
content.english: ℟. Forgive the sin of thy people, O God, and teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and manifest forth thy glory in this place.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Christus perpétuæ det nobis gáudia vitæ.
content.english: Benediction. May Christ to all His people give, for ever in His sight to live.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Sed habitáculum cordis nostri evacuétur vítiis, et virtútibus repleátur; claudátur diábolo, et aperiátur Christo. Et ita labóremus, ut nobis bonórum óperum clávibus iánuam regni cæléstis aperíre possímus. Sicut enim malis opéribus, quasi quibúsdam seris ac véctibus, vitæ nobis ianua claudítur; ita, absque dubio, bonis opéribus aperítur. Et ídeo, fratres caríssimi, unusquísque consíderet consciéntiam suam, et, quando se áliquo crímine vulnerátum esse cognóverit, prius oratiónibus, ieiúniis vel eleemósynis stúdeat mundáre consciéntiam suam; et sic Eucharístiam præsúmat accípere.
content.english: Let the Tabernacle of our heart be swept clean of vices and filled with virtues. Let it be locked to the devil, and thrown open to Christ. Yea, let us so work, that we may be able to open the door of the kingdom of heaven with the key of good works. For even as evil works are so many bolts and bars to close against us the entrance into life, so beyond doubt are good works the key thereto. And therefore, dearly beloved brethren, let each one look into his own conscience, and when he findeth the wounds of guilt there, let him first strive by prayers, fasting, or alms deeds to purge his conscience, and so let him dare to take the Eucharist.

content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: * Surely this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

content.latin: 90:1 Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.

content.latin: 90:3 Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
content.english: 90:3 For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: * and from the sharp word.

content.latin: 90:4 Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.
content.english: 90:4 He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: * and under his wings thou shalt trust.

content.latin: 90:5 Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,
content.english: 90:5 His truth shall compass thee with a shield: * thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

content.latin: 90:6 A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.

content.latin: 90:7 Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
content.english: 90:7 A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand: * but it shall not come nigh thee.

content.latin: In illo témpore: Ingréssus Iesus perambulábat Iéricho. Et ecce vir nómine Zachǽus: et hic princeps erat publicanórum, et ipse dives. Et réliqua.
content.english: At that time: Jesus entered and passed through Jericho. And, behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich. And so on.

content.latin: Homilía sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi
content.english: Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop of Milan.

content.latin: Lib. 8 in Luc., prope finem
content.english: Bk. viii. on Luke.

content.latin: Zachǽus, statúra pusíllus, hoc est, nulla nobilitátis ingénitæ dignitáte sublímis, exíguus méritis sicut pópulus natiónum, audíto Dómini Salvatóris advéntu, quem sui non recéperant, vidére cupiébat. Sed nemo fácile Iesum videt; nemo potest Iesum vidére constitútus in terra. Et, quia non prophétas, non legem habébat, tamquam formæ grátiam naturális, ascéndit in sycómorum, vanitátem scílicet Iudæórum vestígio suo próterens, erráta quoque córrigens superióris ætátis. Et ídeo Iesum in interióris domus recépit hospítio.
content.english: Zacchaeus was little of stature, that is, he was not raised aloft among men by nobility of birth, and, like the most of the world, he possessed few merits. When he heard that the Lord and Saviour, Who had come unto His Own, and Whom His Own had not received, John i. 11, was coming, he desired to see Him. But the sight of Jesus is not easy; to any on the earth it is impossible. And since Zacchaeus had neither the Prophets, nor yet the Law, as a gracious help to his nature, he climbed up into a sycamore tree, raising his feet above the vanity of the Jews, and straightening the crooked branches of his former life, and therefore he received Jesus to lodge within his house.

content.latin: Et bene ascéndit in árborem, ut arbor bona bonos fructus fáceret, ac, naturáli excísus oleástro et contra natúram insértus in bonam olívam, fructum posset legis afférre. Radix enim sancta, etsi rami inútiles. Quorum infructuósam glóriam plebs géntium, fide resurrectiónis, quasi quadam córporis elevatióne, transcéndit. Zachǽus ergo in sycómoro, cæcus in via: quorum álterum Dóminus miseratúrus exspéctat, álterum mansiónis suæ claritáte nobílitat; álterum sanatúrus intérrogat, apud álterum se, non invitátus, invítat. Sciébat enim úberem hospítii sui esse mercédem. Sed tamen, etsi nondum vocem invitántis audíerat, iam víderat afféctum.
content.english: He did well to climb up into a tree, that a good tree might bring forth good fruits, Matth. vii. 17, and that the slip of the wild olive, grafted, contrary to nature, into the good olive, might bring forth the fruits of the law. Rom. xi. 17, 24. For the root is holy, however unprofitable the branches. Their barren beauty hath now been overshadowed by the belief of the Gentiles in the Resurrection, as by a material upgrowth. Zacchaeus, then, was in the sycamore tree, and the blind man by the way-side, xviii. 35. For the one, Jesus stood waiting to show mercy, and asked him before He healed him, what he would that He should do for him; being unbidden of the other, He bade Himself to be his Guest, knowing how rich was the reward of receiving Him. Nevertheless, albeit He had heard no words of invitation, yet had He seen how his heart went.

content.latin: Verum, ne cæcum illum, tamquam fastidiósi páuperum, cito reliquísse videámur et transísse ad dívitem, exspectémus eum, quia exspectávit et Dóminus; interrogémus eum, quia interrogávit et Christus. Nos interrogémus, quia nescímus: ille, quia nóverat. Nos interrogémus, ut sciámus unde iste curátus sit: ille interrogávit, ut in uno plures discerémus unde Dóminum vidére mereámur. Interrogávit enim, ut crederémus, néminem, nisi confiténtem, posse salvári.
content.english: But lest we should seem haughtily to pass by the poor blind man, and to hurry on to the rich one, let us stand waiting for him, as the Lord stood and waited; let us ask of him, as Christ asked of him. Let us ask, because we are ignorant; Christ asked, because He knew. Let us ask, that we may know whence he received his cure; Christ asked, that all of us may know from one example where through we are to earn a sight of the Lord. Christ asked, that we might believe that none, save they that confess Him, can be saved.

content.latin: Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
content.english: All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.

content.latin: Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
content.english: To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.

content.latin: Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
content.english: To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
content.english: bow head Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;

content.latin: Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.

content.latin: Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
content.english: The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
content.english: The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
content.english: The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.

content.latin: Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
content.english: The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;

content.latin: Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
content.english: The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.

content.latin: Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
content.english: Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;

content.latin: Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
content.english: Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.

content.latin: Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
content.english: Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.

content.latin: Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
content.english: Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
content.english: During the following verse all make a profound bow: When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.

content.latin: Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
content.english: When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.

content.latin: Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
content.english: Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.

content.latin: Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
content.english: We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.

content.latin: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
content.english: Kneel for the following verse We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: In Anniversario Dedicationis Ecclesiæ
content.english: Prayer on the anniversary of the dedication:

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis per síngulos annos huius sancti templi tui consecratiónis réparas diem, et sacris semper mystériis repræséntas incólumes: exáudi preces pópuli tui, et præsta; ut quisquis hoc templum benefícia petitúrus ingréditur, cuncta se impetrásse lætétur.
content.english: O God, who dost every year bring round unto us again the day whereon this thine holy temple was hallowed, and bringest us again in soundness of body and mind to be present at thine holy worship, graciously hear the supplications of thy people, and grant that whosoever shall come into this thine house to ask good at thine hand, may be rejoiced in the obtaining of all his request.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Domum tuam, Dómine, * decet sanctitúdo in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: Ant. Holiness becometh thine house, * O Lord, for ever.

content.latin: Psalmus 92 [1]
content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

content.latin: 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.
content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: * the floods have lifted up their voice.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up their waves, * with the noise of many waters.

content.latin: 92:4 Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.
content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

content.latin: 92:5 Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever.

content.english: Ant. My house * shall be called the house of prayer.

content.latin: Psalmus 99 [2]
content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

content.latin: 99:2 Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.
content.english: 99:2 Come in before his presence * with exceeding great joy.

content.latin: 99:3 Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.
content.english: 99:3 Know ye that the Lord he is God: * he made us, and not we ourselves.

content.latin: 99:3 Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.
content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. My house shall be called the house of prayer.

content.latin: Ant. Hæc est domus Dómini * fírmiter ædificáta, bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.
content.english: Ant. This is the Lord's house * stoutly builded, well founded upon a sure rock.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

content.latin: Canticum Trium Puerorum [4]
content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

content.latin: Ant. Bene fundáta est domus Dómini supra firmam petram.
content.english: Ant. The Lord's house is well founded upon a sure rock.

content.latin: Ant. Lápides pretiósi * omnes muri tui, et turres Ierúsalem gemmis ædificabúntur.
content.english: Ant. All thy walls are of stones most precious, * and the towers of Jerusalem shall be built up with jewels.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

content.english: I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a Bride adorned for her husband.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

content.latin: Alto ex Olýmpi vértice
content.english: From highest heaven, the Father's Son,

content.latin: Summi Paréntis Fílius,
content.english: Descending like that mystic stone

content.latin: Ceu monte deséctus lapis
content.english: Cut from a mountain without hands,

content.latin: Terras in imas décidens,
content.english: Came down below, and filled all lands;

content.latin: Domus supérnæ et ínfimæ
content.english: Uniting, midway in the sky,

content.latin: Utrúmque iunxit ángulum.
content.english: His house on earth, and house on high.

content.latin: Sed illa sedes cǽlitum
content.english: That house on high,  it ever rings

content.latin: Semper resúltat láudibus,
content.english: With praises of the King of kings;

content.latin: Deúmque trinum et únicum
content.english: Forever there, on harps divine,

content.latin: Iugi canóre prǽdicat:
content.english: They hymn th' eternal One and Trine;

content.latin: Illi canéntes iúngimur
content.english: We, here below, the strain prolong,

content.latin: Almæ Siónis ǽmuli.
content.english: And faintly echo Sion's song.

content.latin: Hæc templa, Rex cæléstium,
content.english: O Lord of lords invisible!

content.latin: Imple benígno lúmine:
content.english: With thy pure light this temple fill:

content.latin: Huc, o rogátus, ádveni,
content.english: Hither, oft as invoked, descend;

content.latin: Plebísque vota súscipe,
content.english: Here to thy people's prayer attend;

content.latin: Et nostra corda iúgiter
content.english: Here, through all hearts, forevermore,

content.latin: Perfúnde cæli grátia.
content.english: thy Spirit's quick'ning graces pour.

content.latin: Hic ímpetrent fidélium
content.english: Here may the faithful, day by day,

content.latin: Voces precésque súpplicum
content.english: Their hearts' adoring homage pay;

content.latin: Domus beátæ múnera,
content.english: And here receive from thy dear love

content.latin: Partísque donis gáudeant:
content.english: The blessings of that home above;

content.latin: Donec, solúti córpore,
content.english: Till loosened from this mortal chain,

content.latin: Sedes beátas ímpleant.
content.english: Its everlasting joys they gain.

content.latin: Decus Parénti débitum
content.english: To God the Father, glory due

content.latin: Sit usquequáque Altíssimo,
content.english: Be paid by all the heavenly host;

content.latin: Natóque Patris único,
content.english: And to his only Son most true;

content.latin: Et ínclito Paráclito,
content.english: With thee, O mighty Holy Ghost!

content.latin: Cui laus, potéstas, glória
content.english: To whom, praise, power, and blessing be,

content.latin: Ætérna sit per sǽcula.
content.english: Through th' ages of eternity,

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Hæc est domus Dómini fírmiter ædificáta.
content.english: ℣. This is the house of God, stoutly builded.

content.latin: ℟. Bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.
content.english: ℟. Well founded upon a sure rock.

content.latin: Ant. Zachǽe, * festínans descénde, quia hódie in domo tua opórtet me manére. At ille festínans descéndit, et suscépit illum gaudens in domum suam. Hódie huic dómui salus a Deo facta est, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must abide at thy house. * And he made haste and came down, and received Him joyfully into his house. This day is salvation come from God to this house. Alleluia.

content.latin: Canticum Zachariæ
content.english: Canticle of Zacharias

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: In Anniversario Dedicationis Ecclesiæ
content.english: Prayer on the anniversary of the dedication:

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis per síngulos annos huius sancti templi tui consecratiónis réparas diem, et sacris semper mystériis repræséntas incólumes: exáudi preces pópuli tui, et præsta; ut quisquis hoc templum benefícia petitúrus ingréditur, cuncta se impetrásse lætétur.
content.english: O God, who dost every year bring round unto us again the day whereon this thine holy temple was hallowed, and bringest us again in soundness of body and mind to be present at thine holy worship, graciously hear the supplications of thy people, and grant that whosoever shall come into this thine house to ask good at thine hand, may be rejoiced in the obtaining of all his request.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Commemoratio In Commemoratione S. Pauli Apostoli
content.english: Commemoration of Commemoration of St. Paul the Apostle

content.latin: Ant. Vos qui secúti estis me, sedébitis super sedes, iudicántes duódecim tribus Israël, dicit Dóminus.
content.english: Ant. Thus saith the Lord: Ye, which have followed Me, shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Tu es vas electiónis, sancte Paule Apóstole.
content.english: ℣. O Holy Apostle Paul, thou art a chosen vessel unto God.

content.latin: ℟. Prædicátor veritátis in univérso mundo.
content.english: ℟. To preach the Gospel throughout the whole world.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui multitúdinem géntium beáti Pauli Apóstoli prædicatióne docuísti: da nobis, quǽsumus; ut, cuius natalícia cólimus, eius apud te patrocínia sentiámus.
content.english: O God, Who, through the preaching of the Blessed Apostle Paul, hast caused the light of the Gospel to shine gloriously among the Gentiles, we beseech thee that we who keep the Feast of his birth, may, now that he is with thee, feel to our comfort that his prayer availeth much with thee.

content.latin: Commemoratio S. Petri Apostoli
content.english: Commemoration of St. Peter the Apostle

content.latin: Deus, qui beáto Petro Apóstolo tuo, collátis clávibus regni cæléstis, ligándi atque solvéndi pontifícium tradidísti: concéde; ut, intercessiónis eius auxílio, a peccatórum nostrórum néxibus liberémur:
content.english: O God, Who hast given unto thy Blessed Apostle Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and the power to bind and to loose, loose us, we beseech thee, at his mighty intercession, from all the bands of our sins.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: Iam lucis orto sídere,
content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.latin: Deum precémur súpplices,
content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Ant. Holiness becometh thine house, * O Lord, for ever.

content.english: Psalm 53 [1]

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

content.latin: 118:1 (Aleph) Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
content.english: 118:1 (Aleph) Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.

content.latin: 118:2 Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
content.english: 118:2 Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.

content.latin: 118:3 Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
content.english: 118:3 For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.

content.latin: 118:4 Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
content.english: 118:4 Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.

content.latin: 118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
content.english: 118:5 O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:6 Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:6 Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:7 Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:7 I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.

content.latin: 118:8 Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
content.english: 118:8 I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.

content.latin: 118:9 (Beth) In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:9 (Béth) By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.

content.latin: 118:10 In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:10 With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:11 In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
content.english: 118:11 Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.

content.latin: 118:12 Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:12 Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:13 In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.
content.english: 118:13 With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.

content.latin: 118:14 In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
content.english: 118:14 I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.

content.latin: 118:15 In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
content.english: 118:15 I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.

content.latin: 118:16 In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:16 I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:17 (Ghimel) Retríbue servo tuo, vivífica me: * et custódiam sermónes tuos:
content.english: 118:17 (Ghimel) Give bountifully to thy servant, enliven me * and I shall keep thy words.

content.latin: 118:18 Revéla óculos meos: * et considerábo mirabília de lege tua.
content.english: 118:18 Open thou my eyes: * and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law.

content.latin: 118:19 Íncola ego sum in terra: * non abscóndas a me mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:19 I am a sojourner on the earth: * hide not thy commandments from me.

content.latin: 118:20 Concupívit ánima mea desideráre iustificatiónes tuas, * in omni témpore.
content.english: 118:20 My soul hath coveted to long for thy justifications, * at all times.

content.latin: 118:21 Increpásti supérbos: * maledícti qui declínant a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:21 Thou hast rebuked the proud: * they are cursed who decline from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:22 Aufer a me oppróbrium, et contémptum: * quia testimónia tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:22 Remove from me reproach and contempt: * because I have sought after thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:23 Étenim sedérunt príncipes, et advérsum me loquebántur: * servus autem tuus exercebátur in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:23 For princes sat, and spoke against me: * but thy servant was employed in thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:24 Nam et testimónia tua meditátio mea est: * et consílium meum iustificatiónes tuæ.
content.english: 118:24 For thy testimonies are my meditation: * and thy justifications my counsel.

content.latin: 118:25 (Daleth) Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:25 (Daleth) My soul hath cleaved to the pavement: * quicken thou me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:26 Vias meas enuntiávi, et exaudísti me: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:26 I have declared my ways, and thou hast heard me: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:27 Viam iustificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me: * et exercébor in mirabílibus tuis.
content.english: 118:27 Make me to understand the way of thy justifications: * and I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works.

content.latin: 118:28 Dormitávit ánima mea præ tǽdio: * confírma me in verbis tuis.
content.english: 118:28 My soul hath slumbered through heaviness: * strengthen thou me in thy words.

content.latin: 118:29 Viam iniquitátis ámove a me: * et de lege tua miserére mei.
content.english: 118:29 Remove from me the way of iniquity: * and out of thy law have mercy on me.

content.latin: 118:30 Viam veritátis elégi: * iudícia tua non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:30 I have chosen the way of truth: * thy judgments I have not forgotten.

content.latin: 118:31 Adhǽsi testimóniis tuis, Dómine: * noli me confúndere.
content.english: 118:31 I have stuck to thy testimonies, O Lord: * put me not to shame.

content.latin: 118:32 Viam mandatórum tuórum cucúrri, * cum dilatásti cor meum.
content.english: 118:32 I have run the way of thy commandments, * when thou didst enlarge my heart.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: 118:33 (He) Legem pone mihi, Dómine, viam iustificatiónum tuárum: * et exquíram eam semper.
content.english: 118:33 (He) Set before me for a law the way of thy justifications, O Lord: * and I will always seek after it.

content.latin: 118:34 Da mihi intelléctum, et scrutábor legem tuam: * et custódiam illam in toto corde meo.
content.english: 118:34 Give me understanding, and I will search thy law; * and I will keep it with my whole heart.

content.latin: 118:35 Deduc me in sémitam mandatórum tuórum: * quia ipsam vólui.
content.english: 118:35 Lead me into the path of thy commandments; * for this same I have desired.

content.latin: 118:36 Inclína cor meum in testimónia tua: * et non in avarítiam.
content.english: 118:36 Incline my heart into thy testimonies * and not to covetousness.

content.latin: 118:37 Avérte óculos meos ne vídeant vanitátem: * in via tua vivífica me.
content.english: 118:37 Turn away my eyes that they may not behold vanity: * quicken me in thy way.

content.latin: 118:38 Státue servo tuo elóquium tuum, * in timóre tuo.
content.english: 118:38 Establish thy word to thy servant, * in thy fear.

content.latin: 118:39 Ámputa oppróbrium meum quod suspicátus sum: * quia iudícia tua iucúnda.
content.english: 118:39 Turn away my reproach, which I have apprehended: * for thy judgments are delightful.

content.latin: 118:40 Ecce, concupívi mandáta tua: * in æquitáte tua vivífica me.
content.english: 118:40 Behold I have longed after thy precepts: * quicken me in thy justice.

content.latin: 118:41 (Vav) Et véniat super me misericórdia tua, Dómine: * salutáre tuum secúndum elóquium tuum.
content.english: 118:41 (Vau) Let thy mercy also come upon me, O Lord: * thy salvation according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:42 Et respondébo exprobrántibus mihi verbum: * quia sperávi in sermónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:42 So shall I answer them that reproach me in any thing; * that I have trusted in thy words.

content.latin: 118:43 Et ne áuferas de ore meo verbum veritátis usquequáque: * quia in iudíciis tuis supersperávi.
content.english: 118:43 And take not thou the word of truth utterly out of my mouth: * for in thy words, I have hoped exceedingly.

content.latin: 118:44 Et custódiam legem tuam semper: * in sǽculum et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 118:44 So shall I always keep thy law, * for ever and ever.

content.latin: 118:45 Et ambulábam in latitúdine: * quia mandáta tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:45 And I walked at large: * because I have sought after thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:46 Et loquébar in testimóniis tuis in conspéctu regum: * et non confundébar.
content.english: 118:46 And I spoke of thy testimonies before kings: * and I was not ashamed.

content.latin: 118:47 Et meditábar in mandátis tuis, * quæ diléxi.
content.english: 118:47 I meditated also on thy commandments, * which I loved.

content.latin: 118:48 Et levávi manus meas ad mandáta tua, quæ diléxi: * et exercébar in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:48 And I lifted up my hands to thy commandments, which I loved: * and I was exercised in thy justifications.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:49 (Zai) Memor esto verbi tui servo tuo, * in quo mihi spem dedísti.
content.english: 118:49 (Zai) Be thou mindful of thy word to thy servant, * in which thou hast given me hope.

content.latin: 118:50 Hæc me consoláta est in humilitáte mea: * quia elóquium tuum vivificávit me.
content.english: 118:50 This hath comforted me in my humiliation: * because thy word hath enlivened me.

content.latin: 118:51 Supérbi iníque agébant usquequáque: * a lege autem tua non declinávi.
content.english: 118:51 The proud did iniquitously altogether: * but I declined not from thy law.

content.latin: 118:52 Memor fui iudiciórum tuórum a sǽculo, Dómine: * et consolátus sum.
content.english: 118:52 I remembered, O Lord, thy judgments of old: * and I was comforted.

content.latin: 118:53 Deféctio ténuit me, * pro peccatóribus derelinquéntibus legem tuam.
content.english: 118:53 A fainting hath taken hold of me, * because of the wicked that forsake thy law.

content.latin: 118:54 Cantábiles mihi erant iustificatiónes tuæ, * in loco peregrinatiónis meæ.
content.english: 118:54 Thy justifications were the subject of my song, * in the place of my pilgrimage.

content.latin: 118:55 Memor fui nocte nóminis tui, Dómine: * et custodívi legem tuam.
content.english: 118:55 In the night I have remembered thy name, O Lord: * and have kept thy law.

content.latin: 118:56 Hæc facta est mihi: * quia iustificatiónes tuas exquisívi.
content.english: 118:56 This happened to me: * because I sought after thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:57 (Heth) Pórtio mea, Dómine, * dixi custodíre legem tuam.
content.english: 118:57 (Heth) O Lord, my portion, * I have said, I would keep thy law.

content.latin: 118:58 Deprecátus sum fáciem tuam in toto corde meo: * miserére mei secúndum elóquium tuum.
content.english: 118:58 I entreated thy face with all my heart: * have mercy on me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:59 Cogitávi vias meas: * et convérti pedes meos in testimónia tua.
content.english: 118:59 I have thought on my ways: * and turned my feet unto thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:60 Parátus sum, et non sum turbátus: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:60 I am ready, and am not troubled: * that I may keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:61 Funes peccatórum circumpléxi sunt me: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:61 The cords of the wicked have encompassed me: * but I have not forgotten thy law.

content.latin: 118:62 Média nocte surgébam ad confiténdum tibi, * super iudícia iustificatiónis tuæ.
content.english: 118:62 I rose at midnight to give praise to thee; * for the judgments of thy justification.

content.latin: 118:63 Párticeps ego sum ómnium timéntium te: * et custodiéntium mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:63 I am a partaker with all them that fear thee, * and that keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:64 Misericórdia tua, Dómine, plena est terra: * iustificatiónes tuas doce me.
content.english: 118:64 The earth, O Lord, is full of thy mercy: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
